recentItems.title: Family is challenging Ramaphosa’s decision to recognise Queen Masalanabo Modjadji VII as monarch
recentItems.description:
The Modjadji Royal Family's legal battle is continuing at the High Court in Pretoria. The Balobedu royal family says President Cyril Ramaphosa followed instructions from a royal council and other people who had no legal authority.

SABC News Reporter Pimani Baloyi is in Pretoria and joins us live.

recentItems.title: 'Cat' Matlala and co-accused back in court
recentItems.description:
Vusimuzi Matlala and four others are expected back in the High Court in Johannesburg for continuation of trial. 
The main trial has paused to allow for a trial within a trial. 

This because the first accused is objecting to the state using some of the evidence police obtained during his arrest.
 
He argues that the evidence was obtained unlawfully because police did not have a search warrant and they assaulted him. 

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: Throne Battle | Royal family wants the queen's brother recognised as Balobedu monarch
recentItems.description:
The Modjadji Royal Family's legal battle is expected to return to the High Court in Pretoria this morning. The Balobedu royal family says President Cyril Ramaphosa followed instructions from a royal council and other people who had no legal authority. In December 2024, Ramaphosa recognised Queen Masalanabo Modjadji VII as the Balobedu monarch. The family has asked the High Court to cancel his decision. They want the Queen's brother to become the Balobedu monarch.

The family's representative, Advocate Henk Havenga, has asked the court to oversee the creation of a committee to investigate the matter.

SABC News Reporter Pimani Baloyi is in Pretoria and joins us live.

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: 20th Annual Competition Law, Economic and Policy Conference
recentItems.description:
The Competition Commission is hosting the 20th Annual Competition Law, Economic and Policy Conference at Melrose Arch, north of Johannesburg. The conference is being held under the theme Competition Policy for Structural Transformation: Building inclusive, resilient and competitive African markets. The Commission is expected to launch its first ever rural and township economy research report. For more we cross to our reporter Naledi Mabitsela-Ngcobo

recentItems.title: Families of Sharpville Massacre victims and survivors take the state to court
recentItems.description:
Families of the victims and survivors of the Sharpeville Massacre are taking the state to court.

They have filed a class action lawsuit against the state, demanding justice, accountability and compensation.

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: Stats SA | Burglary victims not reporting crimes as they've lost confidence in police response
recentItems.description:
A disturbing warning about public confidence in policing. The latest Stats SA Governance, Public Safety and Justice survey 25/26 says housebreaking remains the most common household crime in the country. But what is perhaps even more concerning is what happens after people are victimised. Only 48% of victims reported the crime, with the rest opting not to report because they don't believe police would do anything about it. 
Let's bring in Snr Coordinator at the Institute for Security Studies, Willem Els.

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: Trial-within-a-trial of Vusimuzi 'Cat' Matlala and co-accused continues
recentItems.description:
The High Court in Johannesburg has heard that the alleged gunman in the attempted murder case of Vusimuzi Matlala and others had allegedly called someone to forcefully take him out of hospital. Musa Kekana was admitted to the Edenvale Hospital in Ekurhuleni under police guard - after he needed medical attention during his 2024 arrest.

For more, we cross to our reporter Neria Hlakotsa.

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: Ngcobo report found Ramaphosa may have violated his oath of office in Phala Phala saga
recentItems.description:
The hearing of President Cyril Ramaphosa's application to review the Section 89 Independent Panel report continues in the Western Cape High Court.

He wants the court to set aside the report which found strong evidence that he may have violated his oath of office regarding the theft at his Phala Phala farm. Yesterday, lawyers representing Ramaphosa argued that the panel had applied the wrong legal standard. 

The nine respondents include some political parties represented in Parliament - as well as National Assembly Speaker Thoko Didiza. 

SABC News Reporter Abra Barbier is in Cape Town and joins us live.

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.
